html:
The Dilmun burial mounds are tens of thousands of earth and stone tombs built across the north of Bahrain, mostly between about 2200 and 1750 BCE, when the island was the heart of Dilmun.

Most are small graves for ordinary people. Near the village of A'ali stand much larger royal mounds, some several metres high. Grave goods show trade with Mesopotamia and the Indus valley.

Many mounds were levelled as modern towns spread after the oil boom. What remains became a World Heritage Site in 2019. With Qal'at al-Bahrain they show that Bahrain was a rich trading place long before pearling or oil.
sum: The Dilmun burial mounds are tens of thousands of earth and stone tombs built across the north of Bahrain, mostly between about 2200 and 1750 BCE, when the island was the heart of Dilmun.
